SEC-CRYPTO-01: Matches hashlib.md5/sha1 and hashlib.new with a literal algorithm name. Misses an algorithm supplied via a variable, config value, or reflection, and cannot distinguish a security use from a benign cache-key or ETag use.
SEC-SECRET-01: Matches an uppercase SECRET/TOKEN/CREDENTIAL identifier assigned a literal of 12+ chars. Misses lowercase or unconventional names, values built by concatenation, credentials in non-Python config files, and short high-value literals below the length floor.
SEC-SQLI-01: Matches concatenation, f-string, percent-format and .format() directly inside an execute() call. Misses a query assembled into a variable on a prior line, built by a helper function, or passed through an ORM raw-SQL wrapper.
SEC-DESER-01: Matches pickle.loads, yaml.load with a single argument, and marshal.loads. Misses aliased imports, yaml.load called with an explicit unsafe Loader keyword, and other deserialisers such as dill, shelve or jsonpickle.
SEC-CMDI-01: Matches os.system and subprocess with shell=True. Misses os.popen, the os.exec family, commands routed through a wrapper utility, and shell=True supplied via kwargs expansion.
SEC-TLS-01: Matches requests with a literal verify=False and the private ssl unverified-context helper. Misses the flag passed as a variable, a session-level assignment, and urllib3 or httpx equivalents.
SEC-RANDOM-01: Flags random.random/randint/choice unconditionally, so it fires on legitimate non-security uses such as retry jitter or sampling. Does not resolve whether the value reaches a security sink; triage accordingly.
